definitions.explanation: An unbroken, continuous line used in diagrams, maps, drawings, road markings, and technical documents. Contrasted with a broken or dashed line.

examples.english: To enclose with a solid line.

examples.japanese: {道路|どうろ}の{白|しろ}い{実線|じっせん}は{車線|しゃせん}{変更|へんこう}{禁止|きんし}を{示|しめ}す。
examples.english: A white solid line on the road indicates that lane changing is prohibited.

examples.japanese: グラフでは{実線|じっせん}が{実績|じっせき}を、{破線|はせん}が{予測|よそく}を{表|あらわ}している。
examples.english: In the graph, the solid line represents actual results and the dashed line represents projections.

notes:
A compound of {実|じつ} (solid, actual) and {線|せん} (line). Note this is a homophone of {実戦|じっせん} (actual combat) and {実践|じっせん} (practice, implementation), but the meaning is entirely different.

USAGE:
Used in technical drawing, graphic design, road markings, maps, and chart/graph descriptions. On Japanese roads, crossing a {実線|じっせん} (solid line) is generally prohibited, while crossing a {破線|はせん} (dashed line) may be permitted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実線|じっせん}で{描|えが}く — to draw with a solid line
- {実線|じっせん}で{囲|かこ}む — to enclose with a solid line
- {白|しろ}い{実線|じっせん} — white solid line (road marking)
- {実線|じっせん}と{破線|はせん} — solid line and dashed line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {破線|はせん} — dashed line, broken line; the contrasting line type
- {点線|てんせん} — dotted line; a line made of dots
- {二重線|にじゅうせん} — double line; two parallel lines
